comments.text: I bought a 54 acre mountain investment property near El Tambo, Loja.  It was low cost, has a fantastic view, power, water, cell service and a road to get to it. I am not a resident but it's great place to come to.  I still have not been to the Amazon or Galapagos but I will next time I go there.  So far, so good.

comments.author: @raysp8026
comments.text: A fair view of Ecuador, warts and all. We have a home in Cuenca and feel very comfortable there. Admittedly, we live in an upscale and established neighborhood which is my one critique of the video. Most of the video was shot in the downtown areas so you do not get a presentation in Cuenca of Gringolandia, Puertas del Sol, El Vergel, all of which are more modern parts of the city with fabulous restaurants, coffee shops, gyms, hospitals etc. I have tested and can attest to the quality of the hospitals and healthcare - really good - however, public system has some challenges. Food / fruit / local markets are fantastic - explore Feria Libre, it is huge. We have visited and spent time in Manta, Montanita, Olon, Mindo, Otavalo, Cotopaxie and Quito and felt safe in all spots. Just need to exercise the usual precautions. Beaches are spectacular with miles of firm sand to walk on. We installed solar system to protect against future droughts and power shortages. but most newer modern apartment blocks have back up generators. We live VERY comfortably on $2,500 per month as a couple eating out whenever we choose, nice gym memberships, classes for art and language etc. There is a tremendous amount of building taking place in Cuenca which we see as a little negative but one cannot stand in the way of progress. Hope this is of interest to some! Cheers.

comments.text: Nice vid! Visited in 2025 to Quito and Galapagos. No problem with safety. Super nice people. Everything is reasonably priced. replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text:
It’s great to hear you felt safe in Quito and the Galápagos and had such a positive impression of the people and prices. A longer trip to explore the cloud forest and Amazon region sounds wonderful.
And thank you for catching the Inti Festival footage issue. You’re absolutely right that some of those visuals are from Cusco, Peru, even though Inti Raymi and related Andean traditions are also celebrated in Ecuador. We really appreciate you pointing that out—we’ll be more careful with regional footage in future videos.
